author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: PKD's earliest completed novel: three Americans left behind to hand over a Chinese industrial site to the advancing Communists, waiting in limbo while their entangled pasts surface.
page_summary:
Three employees of an American company are left behind at an industrial site in China to manage its transfer to the incoming Communist forces. Stranded together with nothing to do but wait, Carl, Verne, and Barbara circle one another; the novel moves through flashback into their earlier lives and romantic entanglements, using the enforced idleness to excavate who they have been.

This is a realist, non-science-fiction novel, and one of PKD's very first — written around 1950, before he had published any SF, and unpublished until after his death, appearing in the 1990s. It is apprentice work, closer to the mainstream literary fiction he wanted to write than to anything he became known for, and of primary interest for showing his early preoccupations with love, self-knowledge, and moral hesitation before the science-fiction machinery arrived to carry them.
